![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081209/assets/7eddb6203ccc3eead9a2a89d7868d3206af52be4c269962e33c551ddd3cf08cd.png)

The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-4,4],$ is shown above. It consists of six line segments.  Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[-1,3].$
worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3-(-1)}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
